statements.text: For Section 301 tariff drawback, this often includes proving that the exported goods either match the imported item exactly or meet the substitution criteria at the 8-digit HTS level.
CBP's published position: Section 301 duties are recoverable through drawback, up to 99 percent. No proclamation bars it.
As noted in CSMS Message 19-000050 Pre-TFTEA Substitution Claims: 301/201 duties are refundable, in full, on pre-TFTEA substitution claims.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has confirmed that duties paid under Section 301 are refundable under the Modernized Drawback regulations (19 CFR Part 190), provided the standard conditions for drawback are met.
Section 301 drawback claims are subject to the same general 5-year statute of limitations that applies to most duty drawback filings.
Under U.S. law, duty drawback allows claimants to recover up to 99% of duties, taxes, and fees paid on imported goods—Section 301 tariffs included.
Section 301 duties are recoverable through drawback, up to 99 percent. No proclamation bars it.
